scope_plain: Voters in Congressional District 20 (part of San Antonio)
office_explainer: Your voice in the U.S. House: votes on federal laws, taxes and spending.
why_it_matters: Rep. Joaquin Castro has held the seat since 2013. The district voted for Kamala Harris by 16 points in 2024, per the San Antonio Report.

candidates.background: Army veteran (combat medic, paratrooper, drill sergeant) and former ICU nurse; has practiced law in Texas for over 20 years. Has also been a pastor.

own_words.text: Lists working-family economic opportunity, public safety, and schools that teach basic skills as his top three priorities.
I would treat cost of living as a production problem, not a press-release problem.
Wants merit-based legal immigration "that puts American first, not open borders."

candidates.name: Joaquin Castro
candidates.background: U.S. representative for San Antonio since 2013; now in his eighth term.

own_words.text: Every American should be able to receive the care they need without fear of financial ruin.
Wants to protect the Affordable Care Act, extend health insurance tax credits and expand Medicaid in Texas.
I support comprehensive immigration reform that balances fairness and security and reflects our values.

office_explainer: Your voice in the U.S. House: votes on federal laws, taxes and spending.

Fighting for national concealed carry reciprocity
In the race's one debate, called veteran suicide an "epidemic" and said he would expand Tricare and VA Community Care.

candidates.name: Katy Padilla Stout
candidates.background: Former public school teacher, now a child welfare and education lawyer. On the Bexar County Child Welfare Board since 2017.

own_words.text: Top priorities: lowering costs for working families, affordable health care and investing in public education.
Health care is a human right.
Backs comprehensive immigration reform with a path to citizenship: "Security and humanity are not opposites."

candidates.name: Ben Mendoza
candidates.background: Listed as a mediator; UTEP criminal justice graduate who was earlier a regional director in Newsweek's education division and owned a formal-wear shop (Branch). Ran for El Paso mayor in 2024, El Paso City Council in 2023 and Congress in 2016 and 2018 (Ballotpedia). No campaign website found.

office_explainer: Bexar County's chief felony prosecutor. Also seeks protective orders and removes children from abusive homes.
why_it_matters: Open seat: DA Joe Gonzales is retiring. The office has a case backlog, prosecutor vacancies and a strained relationship with local police, per Texas Public Radio.

candidates.name: Ashley Foster
candidates.background: Felony prosecutor in the Bexar DA's office for more than 11 years, including capital murder and white-collar cases; civil trial lawyer in private practice since 2012.

own_words.text: Would "focus resources on repeat and violent offenders" and assign one prosecutor to each case from start to finish.
Promises to study the backlog's causes in her first 30 days and work to fix them within 60.
Supports diversion programs if they are voluntary and show results: "the diversion program needs to work."

candidates.name: Luz Elena Chapa
candidates.background: Justice on the 4th Court of Appeals for 12 years, then a visiting judge; civil litigator for 12 years before that. Has not worked as a prosecutor.

own_words.text: Top changes: tackle the backlog, especially family violence cases; repair ties with police; prioritize jailing dangerous offenders.
It shouldn't be a criminal crime or considered a crime to have a severe mental illness.
Would form a committee to review possible death penalty cases and seek it "very sparingly."

candidates.name: Jason Wolff
candidates.background: Criminal defense attorney; earlier a Bexar County prosecutor for 10 years and judge of County Court at Law No. 2 for 8 years, elected as a Republican in 2010 and 2014 (San Antonio Report; campaign site). Did not answer the League questionnaire.

own_words.text: "I will bring the talent and training back to the courthouse."
Would "give discretion to the Assistant District Attorneys and support our local law enforcement officers".
"I just want justice and accountability and to get back to the basics of law enforcement."

office_explainer: One of four commissioners who adopt the county budget and tax rate and approve county contracts.

candidates.background: Civil engineer and business leader (Procter & Gamble, NIBCO) and founder of AI and leadership businesses; Holmes High graduate who grew up in Precinct 2.

own_words.text: Priorities: cut taxes through disciplined budgeting, back law enforcement and courts, and fix roads and drainage.
Taxpayers deserve measurable results for every dollar government spends.
Welcomes data centers if they meet clear standards and do not shift costs to residents.

candidates.background: Commissioner since 2019; former state representative (HD-125), San Antonio councilman and SAISD trustee; began as a juvenile prosecutor.

own_words.text: Priorities: roads and drainage for growth, jail accountability with more diversion and treatment, and closer-to-home health care.
Growth should pay for growth.
Says falling property values mean reviewing new spending carefully and protecting core services.
